doc.name: A — cycling catalogue, archive shelving, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: aero road helmet
Category: cycling
Shot programme: archive shelving
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the still-life director on a commercial cycling shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the macro detail insert in an archive shelving treatment.

SUBJECT. A aero road helmet. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Extreme macro on the closure, seam, texture or applicator — product only partly in frame. Shoot on a 40mm normal at f/1.8, framing for diagonal dynamic balance across the frame.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a projected gobo throwing a broken pattern across the background. Stage the product on or against brushed aluminium, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward Eterna-style muted greens with gentle highlight roll-off. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
